newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil announces oil assets swaps.
newsitem.headline: Statoil announces oil assets swaps.

text.p: State-owned Norwegian oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had reached agreement with five oil companies on purchase, sale and swap transactions covering interests in 21 licences on the Norwegian and British continental shelves.
The overall value of the deals was between five and six billion crowns, Statoil said in a statement.

Total resources involved in the transactions are 340 million barrels of oil and 36.5 billion cubic metres of natural gas. British assets with British Petroleum and Chevron. It also was exchanging interests in Norwegian exploration licences with with Norsk Hydro, Elf and Total.
Statoil said it was withdrawing from 11 licences in all, but would remain in nine of them as manager for the state's direct financial interest.

"These transactions help to meet central Statoil goals of strengthening its position in selected core areas of the Norwegian and British continental shelves, and of improving its long-term production profile," Statoil's statement said.

It said the deals would result in its oil reserve base -- measured as a sum of proven and probable reserves -- declining slightly, but its gas resources would be "substantially" increased by more than 20 billion cubic metres.
In terms of current output, Statoil will be trading a production of 40,000 barrels of oil equivalent (boe) per day and would receive a daily production of close to 20,000 boe.
"In addition come interests in three licences with current or emerging development plans," Statoil said.
"It expects these assets to contribute to its goal of reaching and maintaining a total daily output of one million barrels of oil equivalents in 2005."
